daily_reality.summary: Orthodontists see 50-60 patients per day in a fast-paced clinical environment, hopping between chairs. Mix of braces adjustments, aligner check-ins, new patient consultations, and appliance placements. Heavily team-dependent with trained assistants handling most chairside work.
typical_tasks: Morning huddle — review patient charts, plan day's procedures
Bracket bonding and braces placement on new patients
Wire changes and archwire adjustments (most common appointment type)
Clear aligner check-ins — attachment placement, IPR, tracking assessment
Deband appointments — braces removal and retainer delivery
New patient consultations with records (photos, scans, X-rays)
Review 3D scans and digital treatment plans (ClinCheck, etc.)
Treatment planning using cephalometric analysis and digital models
Manage emergencies — broken brackets, poking wires
Staff training and clinical oversight of orthodontic assistants

deadlines.cme_requirements: Varies by state, typically 30-50 hours per cycle

daily_reality.seasonality: Strong seasonal pattern: new patient starts peak in summer (school break) and January (New Year resolutions). Slower during holidays. Orthodontic practices often schedule longer appointments during summer break.

regulatory.summary: Licensed as dental specialists through state dental boards. Board certification through ABO (American Board of Orthodontics) is voluntary but prestigious. Must complete accredited orthodontic residency after dental school.

key_laws.name: State Dental Practice Acts
key_laws.description: Regulate orthodontic licensure, scope of practice, and delegation to assistants

key_laws.name: American Board of Orthodontics (ABO) Certification
key_laws.description: Written Exam (240 questions) + Scenario-based Clinical Exam. First dental specialty board (est. 1929)

key_laws.name: CODA Accreditation
key_laws.description: Commission on Dental Accreditation standards for orthodontic residency programs

requirements: DMD or DDS degree (4 years dental school)
State dental license + orthodontic specialty registration
ABO board certification (voluntary, highly competitive — only 4% residency admission rate)

regulatory.continuing_education: 30-50 CE hours per biennial cycle (varies by state); ABO requires ongoing certification maintenance activities

tools.summary: Digital transformation is central to modern orthodontics. iTero scanning, ClinCheck treatment planning, and 3D printing are standard. Invisalign/clear aligners have fundamentally changed workflow alongside traditional bracket-and-wire systems.

primary_tools.name: iTero Intraoral Scanner
primary_tools.description: High-resolution 3D digital impressions replacing traditional molds, integrates with Invisalign

primary_tools.name: ClinCheck Treatment Planning Software
primary_tools.description: 3D treatment simulation for Invisalign — real-time plan modifications, multiple treatment plan comparison

primary_tools.name: Invisalign Smile Architect
primary_tools.description: Multi-treatment plan comparison, ortho-restorative planning, side-by-side visualization (2025 update)

primary_tools.name: iTero Design Suite
primary_tools.description: In-practice 3D printing workflow for retainers, models, and appliances (2025 innovation)

primary_tools.name: Dolphin Imaging & Management
primary_tools.description: Cephalometric analysis, treatment planning, patient communication, and practice management

primary_tools.name: 3Shape OrthoAnalyzer
primary_tools.description: Digital model analysis, Bolton analysis, space analysis, and virtual setups

secondary_tools: CBCT scanners (for complex cases — impactions, airway, skeletal assessment)
Digital photography systems (Canon, Nikon with ring flash)
Practice management software (Ortho2, Cloud 9, Dolphin Management)
3D printers (Formlabs, SprintRay) for retainers, models, aligners
pain_points: Invisalign ClinCheck workflow can be slow — back-and-forth with technicians
High cost of aligner systems and scanner subscriptions
Integration between different software platforms is poor
Digital records management across multiple systems
Competition from general dentists offering Invisalign for simple cases

terminology.summary: Rich clinical vocabulary combining dental anatomy, biomechanics, and appliance-specific jargon. Heavy use of classification systems (Angle, skeletal) and abbreviations.

terms.Class I/II/III: Angle classification of malocclusion based on molar relationship
terms.malocclusion: Bad bite — teeth don't fit together properly
terms.overbite: Vertical overlap of upper teeth over lower (deep bite)
terms.overjet: Horizontal distance upper teeth protrude beyond lower
terms.crossbite: Upper teeth bite inside lower teeth (anterior or posterior)
terms.open bite: Gap between upper and lower teeth when biting
terms.IPR: Interproximal Reduction — shaving between teeth for space
terms.archwire: Metal wire connecting brackets that guides tooth movement
terms.bracket: Small square bonded to tooth that holds archwire
terms.power chain: Connected elastics to close spaces between teeth
terms.TADs: Temporary Anchorage Devices — mini-screws for anchorage
terms.bonding: Adhering brackets to teeth with dental adhesive
terms.deband: Removing braces at end of treatment
terms.retainer: Appliance worn after treatment to maintain results
terms.ceph: Cephalometric radiograph — lateral skull X-ray for analysis
terms.RPE/expander: Rapid Palatal Expander — widens upper jaw
terms.tracking: How well aligners are fitting/moving teeth as planned
terms.refinement: Additional aligners ordered to fine-tune results

career_psychology.summary: Highly competitive to enter (4% residency admission rate). Rewarding career with strong income but facing market pressures from DTC aligners and GP competition. Business skills increasingly important alongside clinical expertise.
career_path: Associate orthodontist (1-3 years, learning the business)
DSO/OSO employment (growing trend, especially for younger orthodontists)
fears: General dentists offering Invisalign for simple cases
Student loan debt ($300K-$500K+ from dental school + residency)
motivation: Transforming smiles — high patient satisfaction and visible results
Strong income potential with practice ownership
Growing children and watching development over 2+ year treatments
Good work-life balance compared to other dental specialties
burnout_factors: High patient volume (50-60 per day) creates hectic pace
Need constant new patient flow (finite treatment timelines)
Keeping up with rapid technology changes

community.summary: Tight-knit specialty community organized around AAO (the primary professional association). Active continuing education through annual sessions, winter conferences, and online learning. Growing online presence.
events: AOS Annual Meeting (September 2025 — Las Colinas, TX)
State and regional orthodontic society meetings

market.summary: US orthodontics market worth $4.1 billion (2026). Job growth projected at 8.1%. Facing disruption from DTC aligners and GP Invisalign providers. DSO employment growing (14% of members). 91% of orthodontists optimistic about 2025 production.
demand_drivers: Aging population seeking orthodontic treatment (adult orthodontics growing)
Social media driving demand for perfect smiles
Clear aligner technology expanding treatable patient pool
Underserved rural areas with limited orthodontic access
market_trends: DSO/OSO employment growing — 14% of members (up from 6% in 2018)
Under-35 orthodontists 28% in DSOs vs 12% for 35+
Direct-to-consumer aligners (mixed results, some companies struggling)
General dentists encroaching on simple aligner cases
Digital workflow and in-office 3D printing reducing lab dependence
